hints: Focus on what each test is really looking for, Fehling's and Tollens' for easily oxidised aldehydes, and alkaline iodine for the methyl carbonyl group.

Identify the three carbonyls first, compound 1 is ethanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$), compound 2 is propanone ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$), and compound 3 is pentan-3-one ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$).
Check the iodoform rule carefully, you need $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$, then match that with aldehyde behaviour to judge every tick and cross.
walkthrough:
**Name the functional groups**

Look at the carbonyls side by side. Compound 1 is an aldehyde, ethanal. Compounds 2 and 3 are ketones, propanone and pentan-3-one.

$$\text{1: CH}_3\text{CHO (aldehyde) , 2: CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 \text{(methyl ketone) , 3: CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3 \text{(non-methyl ketone)}$$

**Apply Fehling's and Tollens'**

These are mild oxidising agents. They oxidise aldehydes but cannot oxidise ketones.

$$\text{RCHO + 2[Ag(NH}_3\text{)}_2\text{]}^+ + 3\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{RCOO}^- + 2\text{Ag(s) + 4NH}_3 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
So compound 1 gives a silver mirror with Tollens' and a brick-red $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$ precipitate with Fehling's. Compounds 2 and 3 give no reaction with either, exactly as predicted.

**Apply alkaline iodine, the iodoform test**

A yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$ forms only if the molecule contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$.

$$\text{RCOCH}_3 + 3\text{I}_2 + 4\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{RCOO}^- + \text{CHI}_3\text{(s) + 3I}^- + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Compound 1 ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$) can react, compound 2 ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$) can react, compound 3 has only $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO-}$ groups so it cannot react. That matches the ticks for 1 and 2 and the cross for 3.

**Conclude which rows are right**

Row 1 is all ticks and is correct. Row 2 is tick, cross, cross and is correct. Row 3 is all crosses and is correct. All three rows are correct predictions.

options.A: Correct. Ethanal gives all three positive results, propanone gives only iodoform positive, and pentan-3-one gives all negative. So rows 1, 2 and 3 are all predicted correctly.
options.B: Incorrect because it leaves out row 3. Students choose this if they think all ketones give iodoform, but pentan-3-one has no $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ group so the cross for alkaline $\text{I}_2$ is correct.
options.C: Incorrect because it leaves out row 2. Students choose this if they confuse propanone with a non-methyl ketone, but $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$ is the classic methyl ketone and definitely gives yellow $\text{CHI}_3$.
options.D: Incorrect because it leaves out row 1. Students choose this if they think ethanal cannot give iodoform because it is an aldehyde, but $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$ contains the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ type unit after reaction and gives $\text{CHI}_3$ as well as positive Fehling's and Tollens' tests.
